clue.text: Take audible steps to strike the ball

parts.note: to strike lightly is to tap
a ball is a formal dance

explanation.surface: A golfer or cricketer walks noisily up to hit the ball.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a sport, but 'ball' is the formal social event, not the thing a player hits.
explanation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: this style of dancing uses metal-tipped shoes so every step is heard.

clue.text: Little Mary showed signs of injury, having fallen

parts.note: little Mary is an old British slang name for the stomach, the tum
someone who bled showed a sign of being hurt

explanation.surface: A small girl called Mary is bruised after taking a fall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' is not a girl: it is an old British nickname for the stomach, popularised by a J. M. Barrie play.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone who has toppled over has fallen.

clue.text: Punch the right clock — it gives nothing away

parts.note: to punch someone is to poke them
clock is British slang for a person's face

explanation.surface: Someone hits the correct timepiece, which betrays no secrets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is British slang for the face, as well as the dial of a timepiece having one.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: an expressionless look that hides what a card player is thinking.

clue.text: Motley attires a jester, perhaps

indicators.note: motley means of mixed, varied make-up, so the letters that follow are mixed up

explanation.surface: A jester is dressed in his traditional multicoloured costume.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Motley' reads as the jester's costume but is the signal to rearrange the letters of 'attires'.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a jester is one kind of professional entertainer or performer.

clue.text: Bound to take tea with one man

parts.note: cha is an informal British word for tea
the Roman numeral for one is I
Ned is a man's name

explanation.surface: Somebody is obliged to have tea with a certain gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound to' reads as 'obliged to', but 'Bound' alone is the definition, meaning tied up.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a prisoner tied up in fetters is shackled.

clue.text: Flask depicted by artist in restaurant

indicators.note: in places the artist's letters inside the letters of the eating place

parts.note: a cafe is a small restaurant
RA is a Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A painter sitting in a restaurant sketches a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts RA inside CAFE; RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a glass bottle for serving wine or water at table.

clue.text: They accompany dancers to fish on Sunday

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to cast a net is one way to fish

explanation.surface: Some companions go with the dancers on an angling trip at the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fish' is a whole phrase, CAST A NET, run together; 'on' stacks it above the S in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: hand-held shells clicked in rhythm by flamenco performers.

clue.text: Collar chap who's a villain

parts.note: a ruff is a frilled Elizabethan collar
Ian is a man's name

explanation.surface: A policeman arrests a man who is a crook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Collar' reads as a verb meaning arrest, but it is the frilled neckwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a violent lawless thug.

clue.text: Anticipate payment for receiving minerals

indicators.note: receiving means the word for payment takes the minerals inside it

parts.note: a fee is a payment for a service
ores are minerals from which metal is extracted

explanation.surface: A mining company expects to be paid on delivery of a shipment of minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receiving' is the container signal; 'for' merely joins the definition to the wordplay, tempting as it is to use its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to predict or expect something before it happens.

clue.text: Running through snow, animals will go quickly

definitions.meaning: creatures crossing snow leave a trail of footprints behind them
the idiom means to leave in a hurry

explanation.definitionFit: Literally leaving a trail of prints, and idiomatically hurrying away.

clue.text: Talking in spite of warning

indicators.note: talking says the word is spoken, and what is heard gives another spelling

parts.note: for can mean in spite of, as in 'for all his money he was unhappy'

explanation.surface: Somebody carries on chatting even though they have been cautioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Talking' is the sound signal: FOR, meaning 'in spite of' as in 'for all that', is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the shout a golfer gives to alert people in the path of a ball.

clue.text: In a word, a rum collection of peers

definitions.meaning: the two words 'a rum' run together as one word name a wild plant, the cuckoo pint
peers are titled nobles, here taken as the men and women of the nobility together

explanation.walkthrough: 'a rum' written as one word is ARUM, the wild plant also called cuckoo pint, whose other common name is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A common name for the wild arum plant, and literally a gathering of noblemen and noblewomen.

clue.text: Having no prospects, cleric imbibes English port

indicators.note: imbibes means drinks in, so the cleric's letters take the other pieces inside

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a senior clergyman's degree
Aden is a seaport in Yemen

explanation.surface: A clergyman with no future drinks fortified wine from England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imbibes' is the container signal, in keeping with the drinking picture; 'port' is a harbour city in Yemen, not the fortified wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: describes a job or situation that leads nowhere.

clue.text: A terrifying experience when man's brought before chief officer, they say

indicators.note: they say tells us the phrase is spoken and heard as a different spelling

parts.note: a chess man is a knight, and a town's chief officer is its mayor: knight then mayor

explanation.surface: A soldier is hauled in front of his commanding officer, a frightening ordeal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'they say' is the sound signal: KNIGHT (a chess man) followed by MAYOR is heard as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a very frightening ordeal, originally a bad dream.

clue.text: Repairman adopts a course by no means direct

indicators.note: adopts means takes in, so the repairman's letters take the next letter inside

parts.note: someone who repairs things is a mender

explanation.surface: A man who fixes things takes a roundabout route.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopts' puts the A inside MENDER; the A of the clue is used as a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a winding, wandering path such as a river bend.

clue.text: Run down gradient out of control, stumble at the end

indicators.note: something out of control is in disorder, so the letters of the word before it are disordered
at the end picks the final letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A runner careers downhill too fast and trips at the bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of control' rearranges GRADIENT to DENIGRAT and 'at the end' adds the last letter of 'stumble'; 'Run down' means disparage, not descend.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to disparage or belittle someone.

clue.text: A sign that pegs are damaged

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: A notice warns that the tent pegs are broken.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaged' rearranges the letters of 'pegs are'; the sign is an omen, not a notice.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an omen or portent of what is to come.

clue.text: Whale displaying some character or quality

indicators.note: displaying some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A whale shows a bit of personality or merit.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a family of large baleen sea mammals including the blue and the fin.

clue.text: After a note that's not counterfeit

parts.note: since means after, as in 'since the war'
re is the second note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A banker checks a banknote and finds it is real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'note' is a musical one, RE of do-re-mi, not paper money.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: genuine and honest, free of pretence.

clue.text: Points amassed by ascetic sect

parts.note: compass points are N, S, E and W; here a string of them, E, S, S, E
more compass points, N, E and S

explanation.surface: A strict religious group builds up a score.
explanation.walkthrough: Every letter is a compass point: E, S, S, E, N, E, S; 'amassed by' just joins them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an ancient Jewish brotherhood known for austere communal living.

clue.text: Formerly called wild

parts.note: ex is a prefix meaning former
cited means called on or summoned, as a witness is

explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: wild with enthusiasm means worked up and agitated.

clue.text: I seem as baffled as a foreigner

indicators.note: baffled means confused, so the letters of the three words before it are confused

explanation.surface: The speaker feels as confused as a visitor from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'baffled' rearranges the letters of 'I seem as'; the second 'as' only joins.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a native of the old kingdom now called Thailand, from a British viewpoint.

clue.text: American president accepted by party? It's doubtful

indicators.note: accepted by means the first two pieces are taken inside the word for party

parts.note: a sect is a party or faction
US is an abbreviation meaning American

explanation.surface: It is uncertain whether the American leader has his party's backing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepted by' is the container signal; 'party' looks political but is a religious faction here.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: as an adjective it means questionable or not to be trusted.

clue.text: Campanologists will introduce some variety

definitions.meaning: bell-ringers perform set sequences in which the order of the bells is altered each time
the idiom means to vary the way something is done

explanation.definitionFit: What bell-ringers do in their art, and an idiom for varying one's routine.

clue.text: You can hear birds brood

indicators.note: you can hear says the birds' name is listened to, giving a word spelt differently

parts.note: mews are gulls, sea birds

explanation.surface: The chirping of a nest of chicks reaches the ear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'You can hear' is the sound signal: MEWS, an old name for gulls, is heard as the answer; 'brood' is a verb, not a clutch of chicks.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to ponder or think deeply about something.

clue.text: It's fashionable being rational about silver

indicators.note: about means the phrase for rational goes round the metal's symbol

parts.note: someone all there is sane and in full possession of their wits
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Taking a sensible view of silver jewellery is the trendy thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps ALL THERE, a colloquial phrase for sane, round AG.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: describes something currently very popular or in vogue.

clue.text: Overcharge for wool

definitions.meaning: slang for swindling someone by making them pay too much
the woolly coat shorn from a sheep

explanation.definitionFit: To swindle a customer, and a sheep's shorn coat.

clue.text: A disciple here and there is converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into something else, so the letters of the two words before it change places

explanation.surface: Scattered around, a follower or two takes up the faith.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is converted' rearranges the letters of 'and there'; 'here' only completes the phrase 'here and there' and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a follower or supporter of a leader or creed.
